Title: [DATA] Local: Step 1 - Add Redis to docker-compose.yml
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-01

**Objective**:
Add Redis service to existing docker-compose.yml for local queue-based aggregation.

**Tasks**:
- Add Redis service to docker-compose.yml
- Configure Redis port (6379)
- Add volume for Redis data persistence
- Update docker-compose documentation

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Redis container starts successfully with `docker-compose up -d redis`
- Redis accessible on localhost:6379
- Redis data persists across container restarts
- Documentation updated

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 2 - Install aggregation dependencies
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-02

**Objective**:
Install required packages for queue-based aggregation (BullMQ, Redis client, Node-cron).

**Tasks**:
- Install `bullmq` package
- Install `ioredis` package
- Install `node-cron` package
- Install `@types/node-cron` dev dependency

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All packages installed in dashboard/package.json
- No dependency conflicts
- TypeScript types available

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 3 - Create aggregation directory structure
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-03

**Objective**:
Create folder structure for aggregation code organization.

**Tasks**:
- Create `dashboard/src/lib/aggregation/` directory
- Create `dashboard/scripts/workers/` directory
- Create `dashboard/scripts/cron/` directory
- Add README.md explaining structure

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Directory structure exists
- README documents purpose of each directory

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 4 - Create queue setup (Redis connection + BullMQ queue)
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-04

**Objective**:
Create queue setup file with Redis connection and BullMQ queue initialization.

**Tasks**:
- Create `lib/aggregation/queue.ts`
- Configure Redis connection (localhost:6379)
- Create aggregation queue with BullMQ
- Add default job options (retries, backoff)
- Add error handling

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Queue connects to Redis successfully
- Queue can be imported and used in other files
- Default job options configured (3 attempts, exponential backoff)

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 5 - Create enqueue function
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-05

**Objective**:
Create function to enqueue aggregation jobs for projects.

**Tasks**:
- Create `lib/aggregation/enqueue.ts`
- Implement `enqueueHourlyAggregation()` function
- Query all projects from database
- Create jobs with projectId, startTime, endTime, granularity
- Add error handling and logging

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function successfully enqueues jobs for all projects
- Jobs contain correct data structure
- Error handling for database queries
- Logging shows number of jobs enqueued

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 6 - Create aggregation utility functions
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-06

**Objective**:
Create utility functions for aggregating raw data (ApiTrace, Log, Crash, Session).

**Tasks**:
- Create `lib/aggregation/utils.ts`
- Implement `aggregateTraces()` function
- Implement `aggregateLogs()` function
- Implement `aggregateCrashes()` function
- Implement `aggregateSessions()` function
- Add helper functions for grouping and calculations

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Functions process raw data and return aggregated results
- Supports hourly and daily granularity
- Handles edge cases (nulls, missing data)
- Unit tests for aggregation logic

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 7 - Create worker process
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-07

**Objective**:
Create worker process that consumes jobs from queue and processes aggregations.

**Tasks**:
- Create `scripts/workers/aggregation-worker.ts`
- Connect to Redis and Database
- Implement job processing logic
- Fetch raw data in batches (10K rows)
- Call aggregation utilities
- Insert aggregates into database
- Update last processed time
- Add error handling and retry logic
- Add progress tracking

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Worker runs continuously
- Processes jobs from queue
- Handles batch processing correctly
- Updates database with aggregates
- Logs progress and errors
- Handles job failures gracefully

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 8 - Create cron scheduler
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-08

**Objective**:
Create cron scheduler using node-cron to trigger enqueue function hourly.

**Tasks**:
- Create `scripts/cron/scheduler.ts`
- Configure node-cron for hourly schedule (every hour at :00)
- Call `enqueueHourlyAggregation()` function
- Add error handling and logging
- Support graceful shutdown

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Scheduler runs every hour
- Successfully calls enqueue function
- Logs execution times
- Handles errors without crashing

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 9 - Add npm scripts for worker and cron
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-09

**Objective**:
Add npm scripts to package.json for easy execution of worker and cron.

**Tasks**:
- Add `worker:aggregation` script
- Add `cron:scheduler` script
- Add `worker:dev` script (with watch mode if needed)
- Update package.json documentation

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Scripts run successfully with `pnpm worker:aggregation` and `pnpm cron:scheduler`
- Scripts use tsx for TypeScript execution
- Documentation updated

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 10 - Create test scripts (enqueue + queue status)
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P2
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-10

**Objective**:
Create test scripts for manual testing of enqueue and queue status checking.

**Tasks**:
- Create `scripts/test-enqueue.ts` - manually trigger enqueue
- Create `scripts/check-queue.ts` - check queue status (waiting/active/completed/failed)
- Add helpful output formatting

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Test scripts run successfully
- Enqueue test creates jobs in queue
- Queue status shows accurate counts

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 11 - Test Redis connection and worker
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-11

**Objective**:
Test complete local setup: Redis → Worker → Database.

**Tasks**:
- Start Redis container
- Verify Redis connection
- Start worker process
- Manually enqueue test job
- Verify worker processes job
- Verify aggregates inserted into database
- Test error scenarios

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Redis accessible
- Worker connects to Redis and Database
- Worker processes jobs successfully
- Aggregates appear in database
- Error handling works

Title: [DATA] Local: Step 12 - Test cron scheduler end-to-end
Body:
**Environment**: Local Development
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-LOCAL-12

**Objective**:
Test complete flow: Cron → Enqueue → Queue → Worker → Database.

**Tasks**:
- Start Redis container
- Start worker process
- Start cron scheduler
- Wait for scheduled execution (or trigger manually)
- Verify jobs enqueued
- Verify jobs processed
- Verify aggregates created
- Test with multiple projects

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Complete flow works end-to-end
- Jobs enqueued automatically
- Jobs processed by worker
- Aggregates created correctly
- Multiple projects handled correctly

Title: [DATA] Production: Step 1 - Set up Upstash Redis (serverless queue)
Body:
**Environment**: Production (Vercel)
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PROD-01

**Objective**:
Set up Upstash Redis for serverless queue in production.

**Tasks**:
- Create Upstash Redis instance
- Get connection credentials (URL, token)
- Add environment variables to Vercel
- Test connection from Vercel functions
- Document connection setup

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Upstash Redis instance created
- Environment variables configured in Vercel
- Connection test successful
- Documentation updated

Title: [DATA] Production: Step 2 - Create Vercel Cron job (enqueue)
Body:
**Environment**: Production (Vercel)
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PROD-02

**Objective**:
Create Vercel Cron job that enqueues aggregation jobs hourly.

**Tasks**:
- Create `api/cron/aggregate-hourly/route.ts`
- Configure vercel.json cron schedule (every hour)
- Implement enqueue logic using Upstash Queue
- Add error handling and logging
- Add authentication/authorization check

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Cron job runs every hour
- Successfully enqueues jobs to Upstash
- Logs execution in Vercel logs
- Handles errors gracefully
- Only runs for authorized requests

Title: [DATA] Production: Step 3 - Set up external worker service (Railway/Render)
Body:
**Environment**: Production (External Service)
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PROD-03

**Objective**:
Deploy worker process to external service (Railway or Render) to process jobs.

**Tasks**:
- Choose service (Railway or Render)
- Create new service/project
- Configure environment variables (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL)
- Deploy worker code
- Set up health checks
- Configure auto-restart on failure
- Set up monitoring/logging

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Worker deployed and running
- Connects to Upstash Redis
- Connects to production database
- Processes jobs successfully
- Health checks configured
- Logs visible in service dashboard

Title: [DATA] Production: Step 4 - Create production queue setup (Upstash)
Body:
**Environment**: Production (Vercel + External Worker)
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PROD-04

**Objective**:
Create queue setup that works with Upstash Redis in production.

**Tasks**:
- Update `lib/aggregation/queue.ts` to support Upstash
- Use `@upstash/redis` or `ioredis` with Upstash URL
- Handle both local (Docker) and production (Upstash) environments
- Add connection retry logic
- Test with Upstash

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Queue works with Upstash Redis
- Environment detection (local vs production)
- Connection retry on failure
- Works in both Vercel functions and external worker

Title: [DATA] Production: Step 5 - Update worker for production (Upstash + Production DB)
Body:
**Environment**: Production (External Worker)
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PROD-05

**Objective**:
Update worker process to work with Upstash Redis and production database.

**Tasks**:
- Update worker to use Upstash Redis connection
- Update worker to use production DATABASE_URL
- Add production-specific error handling
- Add monitoring/metrics (optional)
- Test with production environment

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Worker connects to Upstash Redis
- Worker connects to production database
- Processes jobs correctly
- Error handling works
- Logs properly formatted

Title: [DATA] Production: Step 6 - Test production aggregation end-to-end
Body:
**Environment**: Production
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PROD-06

**Objective**:
Test complete production flow: Vercel Cron → Upstash Queue → External Worker → Production DB.

**Tasks**:
- Trigger Vercel Cron manually (or wait for schedule)
- Verify jobs enqueued in Upstash
- Verify worker picks up jobs
- Verify worker processes jobs
- Verify aggregates created in production DB
- Monitor for errors
- Test with real production data

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Complete production flow works
- Jobs enqueued by Vercel Cron
- Worker processes jobs successfully
- Aggregates created in production database
- No errors in logs
- Performance acceptable

Title: [DATA] Database: Create ProjectAggregationState table
Body:
**Environment**: All
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-DB-02

**Objective**:
Create table to track last processed time for each project (incremental aggregation).

**Tasks**:
- Create Prisma model for ProjectAggregationState
- Fields: projectId, lastHourlyAgg, lastDailyAgg, updatedAt
- Add unique constraint on projectId
- Create migration

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Model created
- Migration applied
- Unique constraint works
- Can track last processed times

Title: [DATA] Performance: Add indexes for raw table queries (Live Debug optimization)
Body:
**Environment**: All
**Priority**: P1
**Sequence**: AGG-PERF-01

**Objective**:
Add indexes to raw tables for fast Live Debug queries (projectId + deviceId + timestamp).

**Tasks**:
- Add composite index on ApiTrace(projectId, deviceId, timestamp DESC)
- Add composite index on Log(projectId, deviceId, timestamp DESC)
- Add composite index on Crash(projectId, deviceId, timestamp DESC)
- Create migration
- Test query performance

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Indexes created
- Live Debug queries use indexes
- Query performance improved
- No negative impact on writes
